subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - follow-up
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finlytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO follow-up (p95/p99)

Thanks again for the call today - good conversation. As promised, attaching our high-level perf summary from Q2 so you have current numbers and the workloads we care about. A few clarifications from our side to help scope a POC:

- End-to-end p95 today (current provider): ~480ms
- End-to-end p99 today (current provider): ~1.2s
- Typical request: chat turn with avg ~256 tokens (incoming + response)
- Concurrency: sustained ~40 concurrent API requests; burst to ~100 during peak traffic windows
- Streaming: yes - the product expects partial tokens to display within ~200ms of acceptance for the first token (so first-byte latency is critical)
- Throughput: ~120k tokens/minute during peak 15-minute windows

We're trying to understand where Redwood's hosted API would land relative to these figures (p95/p99 end-to-end, first-token streaming latency, and how concurrency affects p99).

Attachment: finlytics_perf_summary_q2.csv (CSV)

Next steps from our side: we can set aside engineering hours for a week-long POC in August if we align on acceptance criteria and test harness.

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Engineering, Finlytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up (p95/p99)

Alex - thanks for the summary and the attachment. Quick recap + a couple questions so we can scope a POC and test plan:

Recap of what we heard:
- Target: reduce p95 and p99 end-to-end relative to current provider (we typically aim for p95 <= 350ms and p99 <= 700ms for similar chat workloads on our hosted API).
- Streaming: first-byte within ~200ms is a hard UX requirement.
- Concurrency: sustained ~40, bursts to ~100.

A few clarifying questions so our infra team can size the workload:
1) Can you share the distribution of sequence lengths (token bins: <128, 128-512, >512) - if 256 is the mean, how many requests go above 512?
2) Are the bursts short (seconds) or sustained (minutes)? That affects whether hosted autoscaling or Dedicated capacity is a better fit.
3) For the streaming requirement, is it acceptable to see the first token within 200ms and the rest stream at variable rates, or do you need steady low inter-token latency for the full response?

Action items from Redwood:
- We'll propose an initial acceptance criteria document for the POC (p95/p99 targets, streaming thresholds, concurrency matrix).
- If the requirement is sustained high concurrency with strict p99, we'll scope Dedicated as an option and include baseline pricing.

I attached a short POC plan (outline) and a proposed test harness we often use for similar customers. If you can return the token distribution and burst length details, we'll finalize the POC acceptance criteria and propose dates.

Attachment: redwood_poc_plan.md (Markdown)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finlytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up (p95/p99)

Thanks - quick answers below and a few constraints from our infra team:

1) Token distribution (approx):
- <128 tokens: 18%
- 128-512 tokens: 64%
- >512 tokens: 18% (peaks during long-form summarization)

2) Burst character: typically two kinds:
- Short bursts (30-90s) during feature launches (frontend fan-out)
- Mid bursts (5-20 min) during scheduled batch activations and demos

3) Streaming: first-byte <= 200ms is critical for the chat UX. After the first token we expect reasonably continuous streaming (not hard real-time, but inter-token delays should stay below ~80ms on average to avoid janky UX).

Additional constraints:
- We require TLS mutual-auth for the POC endpoints (mTLS) and an audit-able request log for sampling production traffic during the POC.
- Procurement will need an indicative estimate of monthly cost at sustained 40 concurrency and a 20% buffer for peak.

We're open to a hosted POC initially - if we hit p99 regressions at sustained load we'll discuss Dedicated. Proposed timeframe: 10-14 Aug for POC (we can confirm next week).

—Alex

Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up (p95/p99) - next steps

Alex / Priya - great, thanks for the quick turnaround and the distribution details. Proposed next steps:

1) Quick triage call with our infra lead (Aditya) and your platform engineer to lock down mTLS and sampling/logging details - can we do 45 minutes this Friday (16 Jul) or early next week?
2) Redwood will deliver a POC acceptance criteria doc by EOD Friday (15 Jul) that includes:
   - p95 target: <= 350ms end-to-end
   - p99 target: <= 700ms end-to-end
   - streaming: first-byte <= 200ms; average inter-token <= 80ms during streaming
   - concurrency matrix: sustained 40, bursts to 100 for up to 15 minutes
   - required security: mTLS + sampled request logs (masked PII)
3) We'll nominate test harness and provide an initial runbook. If you're comfortable, we'll run the hosted POC (preferred) and surface Dedicated sizing only if p99 degradation is observed under sustained load.

Please confirm the triage time that works for your engineer. Once we lock that, we'll send calendar invites and the POC acceptance doc.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Marissa.C@redwood.com

summary: Sales follow-up thread to qualify p95/p99 performance SLOs for Finlytics. Discusses current provider baselines, traffic profile (token distribution, concurrency, bursts), streaming requirements (first-byte target and inter-token latency), security (mTLS, sampled logs), and next steps for a hosted POC with acceptance criteria and potential Dedicated sizing.
